chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Rifāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: Do the people depart to Minā in the morning? He said: Yes, until sunset.
So it does not contradict the first report, because this report is to be understood as referring to what we mentioned regarding one who has excuses, the sick person, and others; that indicates this.

key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the first report, with which this narration is being reconciled
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْأَعْذَارِ: a person with valid excuses or impediments
key_terms.غُدْوَةً: in the morning, early part of the day
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, the end point mentioned for permissibility
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the hajj site to which pilgrims depart at a designated time

ai.seo_question: Until what time may people depart to Minā, especially those with valid excuses?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the timing of departure to Minā during hajj and indicates permissibility extending until sunset. The closing clarification explains that the report is understood in relation to people with valid excuses, such as the sick and others in similar circumstances, thereby reconciling it with an earlier report.
